transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2025-05-20 15:30 UTC
Duration: 46 minutes
Attendees: Lena (Redwood AE), Marcus (Redwood SE), Jin (Redwood Support), Priya (Umbratek ML), Daniel (Umbratek Infra), Sarah (PM), Raj (SRE)

Auto-summary (auto-generated, may be noisy):
- Week 3 pilot results reviewed; Redwood shows ~18% lower median latency and 1.6x throughput for the same model compared to BaselineCloudAI under current test harness.
- p99 remains a pain point; contention at KV-cache misses and GPU memory swapping noted.
- Action items: re-run p99 with doubled batching, share raw CSVs, confirm VPC peering window, price for dedicated nodes.

Topics: benchmark numbers, p50/p95/p99, batching, KV cache, quantization effects, routing/fallback, dedicated vs hosted, security (KMS/SOC2)

Transcript body:
[00:00] Lena: Good afternoon everyone, thanks for joining. Quick roll call?
[00:05] Priya: Hey, Priya here.
[00:08] Daniel: Daniel on infra.
[00:11] Sarah: Sarah, product.
[00:13] Raj: Raj, SRE.
[00:15] Marcus: Marcus, Redwood SE.
[00:18] Jin: Jin from support.
[00:20] Lena: Cool, thanks. I'll hand it to Marcus to run through the week 3 numbers. Marcus?
[00:26] Marcus: Yep, thanks. So we ran the benchmark suite you shared last week, the same replay window, same prompt mix — 60% short completions, 30% mid, 10% long. We compared Redwood hosted runner against your baseline provider (BaselineCloudAI) using the same model checkpoint (v1.4-open).
[00:44] Marcus: Top-level summary: median latency (per request) for Redwood was 84ms vs baseline 102ms — so about 18% improvement. Throughput (tokens/sec) averaged 1.6x higher on Redwood under the synthetic load we used. p95 was 230ms vs 290ms, so roughly 20% better. p99 is still close: Redwood 480ms vs baseline 520ms, so only a 7-8% gap.
[01:15] Priya: Wait, can you repeat the p99 numbers? I'm worried about tail latency for our live traffic.
[01:18] Marcus: Sure — Redwood p99 480 milliseconds, baseline 520. But important caveat: the p99 runs had a higher variance depending on KV cache hit rate. When we had prefix/KV cache hits above 78% we saw p99 drop into the mid-300s.
[01:35] Daniel: We saw a few spikes on our side too when tokens-per-request spiked and the GPU swapped some memory; is that visible in your logs?
[01:42] Marcus: Yes, we observed GPU-side memory pressure during long-tail bursts — particularly when quantization fallback triggered for a small fraction of requests. The kernel selection path sometimes falls back to FP16 kernels which cause an allocation step. That's the noisy path.
[01:58] Raj: Is that the quantization threshold you mentioned earlier — like when a request hits a token length above N it goes to a different kernel?
[02:04] Marcus: Exactly. We have heuristics: up to 1024 tokens we use the optimized int8 kernels; beyond that or on certain attention patterns we drift to FP16. That fallback can cost 80–120ms extra on the tail.
[02:18] Priya: Hmm, our customer traffic has ~12% long requests over 1k tokens.
[02:22] Marcus: That's probably the main reason p99 isn't collapsing further. Two levers here: (1) increase KV/prefix cache so fewer long-run recomputes, (2) tune the quantization profile — we can pin the int8 path more aggressively but it risks small quality regressions.
[02:38] Sarah: Quality regressions — can you quantify that? Our product team is sensitive to hallucinations.
[02:43] Marcus: Short answer, in our sanity evals we saw negligible diffs for most prompts, but a few edge-case prompts with rare tokens had small score drops. We tracked that with the eval harness. We can share the diff reports.
[02:54] Priya: Please share. We have a small set of golden prompts we need zero-regression on.
[02:59] Marcus: Noted. We'll include the golden set delta.
[03:02] Lena: Can we walk through the testing harness differences vs BaselineCloudAI? Priya, you initially said you tried to keep them identical.
[03:09] Priya: We used the same replay trace but Baseline's endpoint had slightly different max-concurrency defaults, so we forced a 128 concurrency limit to match. The container images were similar but Baseline was running a slightly older CUDA stack, maybe 11.4 vs your 12.1.
[03:26] Marcus: That can explain a few kernel perf deltas. Also Baseline wasn't doing continuous batching; they had fixed micro-batch sizes per request so high overhead on small requests. Our continuous batching reduced per-request fixed cost.
[03:40] Daniel: On the infra side, we did see one network tail around 03:14 UTC where a chunk retransmit increased latency. Could that have impacted p99?
[03:49] Marcus: Potentially. For p99 we try to filter out network outliers but if it's recurrent during the replay window, it will show up. We'll attach per-request traces so you can correlate.
[03:59] Raj: What's your suggestion on dedicated vs hosted for the pilot? If we go dedicated, does p99 improve considerably?
[04:05] Marcus: Dedicated helps in two ways: guaranteed GPU affinity (no noisy neighbors) and ability to adjust kernel/hot path parameters. In our internal sims, moving to a dedicated pool for the same model reduced p99 by ~22% relative to our hosted baseline in a similar noisy workload. But it depends on the workload — highly bursty long-tail will still need caching strategies.
[04:22] Priya: Any security blockers for dedicated? We need KMS integration and SOC2 artifacts.
[04:26] Lena: We have KMS integrations (AWS KMS, GCP KMS), HSM partner if required, and our SOC2 Type II report is in the shared security pack. We'll push the link after the call.
[04:36] Sarah: Perfect. Also need SAML SSO + SCIM provisioning.
[04:39] Lena: Yep, supported. We'll include the SSO playbook.
[04:43] Jin: On the benchmark artifacts, I'm going to drop the exact bench scripts and Dockerfile into the shared drive right after this call. That should help reproduce the runs.
[04:51] Marcus: Quick note on caching: we saw a big delta in throughput when KV cache hit rate went from 55% to 78% — tokens/sec jumped 1.4x. So improving cache locality in your replay should be high priority.
[05:03] Priya: How do we improve cache locality? Our prompts are user-generated and pretty diverse.
[05:08] Marcus: Two practical ideas: prefix normalization (strip session ids), and short-lived warmers for high-frequency prompts. Also session affinity routing helps so repeated users hit warmed instances.
[05:20] Daniel: We can add a lightweight pre-hash in the API gateway to normalize prefixes. We'll test that in the replay.
[05:26] Raj: On the monitoring side, do you expose per-token cost breakdown and token-level latency?
[05:31] Lena: Yes — Console shows token-level cost, per-route p50/p95/p99, and KV cache hit metrics if you enable the instrumentation hook. We can turn that on for the pilot.
[05:41] Priya: Let's enable it — that will help debug the tail.
[05:44] Marcus: For the p99 rerun action: we'll double batching (2x) and also run a separate run where we pin int8 kernels and another where we allow fallback. That will show the tradeoffs.
[05:56] Sarah: Can you also include a run that simulates our peak hour burst (3x baseline RPS) — we want to see graceful degradation.
[06:02] Marcus: Yes, we'll append a stress test run.
[06:05] Priya: One operational question: if a dedicated host runs out of capacity, do you auto-failover to hosted? We need continuity for customer-facing features.
[06:13] Marcus: We support automated fallback policies — you can configure a route to failover to a compatible model variant on hosted capacity. There's a small latency bump but keeps things up.
[06:23] Daniel: On peering, our security team needs a 2-hour maintenance window to open firewall ports for the VPC peering. Can we schedule that?
[06:30] Lena: We'll coordinate. Daniel, can you propose windows?
[06:33] Daniel: I'll send two options today.
[06:35] Marcus: Quick note on the diff with BaselineCloudAI: they had slightly lower cost per token on their smallest instance but at the cost of higher p95 and more variability. Our conclusion: Redwood gives better predictable tail behavior and better throughput for this workload.
[06:51] Priya: That's consistent with our internal traces. One last ask — can you produce a per-workload cost projection given our RPS and target SLA?
[06:58] Lena: Yes — Lena to send a cost model with ops scenarios (hosted pilot vs dedicated 4x A100 equiv).
[07:06] Priya: Great.
[07:08] Lena: Ok let's recap next steps. Marcus?
[07:11] Marcus: Re-run p99 with 2x batching, pin int8 run, fallback run, and a 3x stress test. Share raw CSVs and per-request traces.
[07:20] Lena: I'll send pricing for dedicated nodes and the security pack (SOC2, SAML guide, KMS notes).
[07:26] Priya: We'll provide traffic replay traces and golden prompt set.
[07:29] Daniel: I'll propose the VPC peering windows and confirm firewall rules.
[07:33] Lena: Anything else?
[07:34] Raj: Nothing from SRE.
[07:36] Sarah: No. Thanks everyone.
[07:38] Lena: Thanks all — we'll follow up in the thread.

End of transcript.
